title: Table Tennis: Spin, Serves, and Stars

blocks.title: Table Tennis: Spin, Serves, and Stars
paragraphs: Table tennis is fast, but small actions can change the ball. Explore spin, a legal serve, the sport’s early days, and two Olympic stars. Watch how simple movements create exciting play.

blocks.title: Spin Changes the Ball
paragraphs: Players brush the ball with the racket to make spin. The three basic kinds are topspin, backspin, and sidespin. Topspin makes the ball dip and move forward quickly after the bounce. Backspin can make it stay low and slow. Sidespin can make it curve left or right. Spin is often hard to see before the bounce. Its effect is easier to see after the ball hits the table. A player watches the bounce and changes the next shot.

images.alt: A table tennis player brushes the ball while three paths show the ball dipping, staying low, and curving.

items.prompt: Which spin can make the ball curve left or right?
items.answer: Sidespin can make the ball curve left or right.
choices: Topspin can make the ball curve left or right.
Backspin can make the ball curve left or right.
Sidespin can make the ball curve left or right.
items.explanation:
Sidespin changes the ball’s path to the left or right.

Which kind of spin would be fun for you to try, and why?

blocks.title: Every Point Starts with a Serve
paragraphs: Every point starts with a serve. In an official serve, the ball begins on an open palm. The server tosses it nearly straight up at least 16 centimetres. The server hits the ball as it falls. The ball first bounces on the server’s side of the table. Then it bounces on the other side. A server can change the speed, place, and spin. These changes can make the next shot difficult. A short backspin serve and a fast topspin serve can start two very different points.

images.alt: Five panels show a table tennis serve from an open palm to two table bounces.

items.prompt: Where does the ball begin in an official serve?

choices: The ball begins under the table.

items.explanation:
The server holds the ball on an open palm before tossing it.

Would you choose a fast serve or a slow, spinning serve? Why?

blocks.title: From a Dining Table to a World Sport
paragraphs: Table tennis began in England in the 1880s. People played it as an indoor form of lawn tennis. They used a dining table and simple equipment they had around them. The sport later became more organised. The International Table Tennis Federation, or ITTF, began in 1926. The first World Championships also took place in 1926, in London. A game for indoor tables had become an international sport. Today, the table is still small, but players compete around the world.

images.alt: An early dining-table game in England changes into modern table tennis.

items.explanation:

Why do you think an indoor table game became popular?

blocks.title: Two Olympic Stars
paragraphs: Ma Long represents China. He won the Olympic men’s singles title in 2016 and again at Tokyo 2020. He became the first man to win this Olympic singles title twice. Mima Ito represents Japan. At Tokyo 2020, she and Jun Mizutani won the first Olympic mixed doubles table tennis title. It was also Japan’s first Olympic gold medal in table tennis. Ma Long’s result shows success across two Olympic Games. Mima Ito’s result marks two important firsts in one event.

items.prompt: What was special about Ma Long’s second Olympic men’s singles title?
items.answer: He became the first man to win the title twice.
choices: He became the first man to win the title twice.
He became the first person to invent table tennis.
He won Japan’s first table tennis gold medal.
items.explanation:
His wins came in 2016 and at Tokyo 2020.

Which result interests you more: Ma Long’s two singles titles or Mima Ito’s two historic firsts? Why?
